beats: A broke student killed a pawnbroker to prove he was a genius, then never spent a single kopek!
It's 1865 in St. Petersburg, and Rodion Raskolnikov lives in a room the size of a cupboard.
This is Crime and Punishment, by Fyodor Dostoevsky.
He has a theory: extraordinary men, like Napoleon, are allowed to step over the law.
So he takes an axe from the porter's lodge and visits the old pawnbroker.
But her sister Lizaveta walks in, and he kills her too!
He hides the loot under a stone in a courtyard, and never even checks how much he took.
Then he falls into a fever for days.
A detective named Porfiry plays cat and mouse with him, but never quite arrests him.
Then a house painter confesses to the murders instead!
Instead, he confesses to Sonya, a poor girl forced onto the streets to feed her family.
She tells him to kiss the ground at the crossroads and turn himself in.
He does, and gets eight years of hard labor in Siberia!
He set out to prove he was Napoleon, and decided he was a louse!
